segments.content: People say you can see the Great Wall of China from space with the naked eye.

matches.claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.

sources.title: NASA: China's Wall Less Great in View from Space
Scientific American: Is China's Great Wall Visible from Space?

matches.claim: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of China. Contrary to a common myth, it is not visible to the unaided eye from low Earth orbit.

segments.content: And another one: humans only use ten percent of their brains.

matches.claim: Humans only use ten percent of their brains.

sources.title: Scientific American: Do People Only Use 10 Percent of Their Brains?

segments.content: Anyway, let me know what you think in the comments.
Here's a classic: lightning never strikes the same place twice.

matches.claim: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
Lightning is a sudden electrostatic discharge during a thunderstorm. Tall, isolated structures are often struck many times during a single storm.

segments.content: People also think goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.

matches.claim: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.

sources.title: Scientific American: Fact or Fiction: Goldfish Memory

segments.content: And to finish, nothing can travel faster than the speed of light in a vacuum.

matches.claim: Nothing can travel faster than the speed of light in a vacuum.
The speed of light in a vacuum, commonly denoted c, is a universal physical constant. No information or matter can travel faster than light in a vacuum.
